Theme

Nature & food

rise verb

of a river or a mountain

also have its source, rise in

classical

Curt. 8.9.3: inclutī amnēs Caucasō monte ortī (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 206

orior, orīrī, ortus sum

verb, fourth conjugation, deponent

rise, have its source (of a river)

Other words

  • exorior, exorīrī, exortus sum

    verb, fourth conjugation, deponent · also used · modern · Traupman 206

    Lewis & Short has it of the sun and stars rising and of things that spring up; we have found no classical instance of a river. Traupman uses it so.

  • surgō, surgere, surrēxī, surrēctum — rise (of a mountain)

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Ov. M. 1.44: lapidōsōs surgere montēs (Lewis & Short); Mela 1.19: mōns Rhīpaeus (Lewis & Short); Traupman 206; of several mountains cōnsurgere

Examples

  • Tiberis monte Appennīnō oriēns

    the Tiber rising in the ApenninesTraupman 206

See also source, river.

SourcesJohn C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency.
